documents.title: Guidelines for the Use of GenAI in Assessments and Deliverables at SDSU
documents.summary: A Senate-adopted four-level scale (AI-1 to AI-4) for GenAI use in assessments, with each instructor required to classify assessments and state the level in the syllabus from Fall 2025. It adds principles of proficiency, verification and documentation, privacy and security advice, citation formats, and 2026 rules that instructors disclose their own AI use.
documents.stance_why: The document sets no single rule: it says 'Instructors shall provide clear instructions for the appropriate level of genAI usage permitted in each of their courses and for each of their assessments, ranging from disallowed to unrestricted', and its AI-1 to AI-4 scheme is a set of tiers, so the stance is delegates.

units.why: The Senate rule that 'all SDSU syllabi shall include a statement' on genAI is a mandatory syllabus-statement requirement addressed to instructors, set at course start; P09 fits exactly.
units.anchor: all SDSU syllabi shall include a statement about how
units.frag_end: may not be used in courses
units.policy: Effective Fall 2025, all SDSU syllabi include a statement about how generative AI may or may not be used in courses.

units.why: 'Instructors shall provide clear instructions for the appropriate level of genAI usage' 'for each of their assessments' leaves the level to the instructor per course and assessment, so P04 rather than P05 (the scale itself is coded separately).
units.anchor: appropriate level of genAI usage permitted in each of their courses
units.policy: Instructors provide clear instructions for the appropriate level of genAI usage permitted in each of their courses and for each assessment, ranging from disallowed to unrestricted.

units.why: The Center for Teaching and Learning supplies 'recommended template language' that instructors 'may use'; this is faculty support, nearest P63, though it is a template rather than a workshop.
units.anchor: may use recommended template language provided by the Center for Teaching and
units.frag_end: as is appropriate to their instructional needs
units.policy: Instructors may use recommended template language provided by the Center for Teaching and Learning, or develop their own as is appropriate to their instructional needs.
units.fit_note: P63 covers workshops and advice; this unit offers ready-made template statement language and permits instructors to write their own.

units.why: This says a missing syllabus statement 'may be considered a factor' when a student is referred for suspected genAI plagiarism, so it links instructor communication to enforcement. It is not a fallback rule for silent syllabi (P06) and no other type covers it, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: absence of a syllabus statement may be considered a factor in cases where a student
units.policy: The absence of a syllabus statement may be considered a factor in cases where a student is referred to the Center for Student Rights and Responsibilities for suspected genAI plagiarism.
units.uncovered_note: A missing syllabus AI statement can weigh in an integrity referral, tying the instructor's duty to communicate to how misconduct cases are judged.

units.why: The Senate 'voted to expand the definition of plagiarism to include' work by generative AI 'as one's own', classifying unauthorized AI-produced work as plagiarism under integrity processes (P36).
units.anchor: definition of plagiarism to include “representing work produced by generative artificial
units.policy: The University Senate expanded the definition of plagiarism to include representing work produced by generative artificial intelligence (AI) as one's own.

units.why: The course-proposal checklist asks whether the syllabus 'include[s] ... AI Syllabus Statement', an administrative review check enforcing the syllabus-statement requirement (P09).
units.anchor: AI Syllabus Statement?
units.frag_start: Does the syllabus include a link
units.policy: Course reviewers check whether the syllabus includes an AI Syllabus Statement.

units.why: The Graduate Council 'recommending all programs develop their own policies' on AI use leaves graduate-student AI rules to each program; it is a recommendation, so should, and P04 (delegation) is nearest.
units.anchor: recommending all programs develop
units.policy: The Graduate Council recommends that all programs develop their own policies on AI use for graduate students.
units.fit_note: Delegation is to graduate programs, not to instructors or assignments.

units.why: Instructors 'shall disclose to their students generative use of AI in the creation of instructional materials': AI-made materials are disclosed, so P48, though review is not mentioned.
units.anchor: shall disclose to their students generative use of AI in the creation of
units.policy: Instructors of record disclose to their students generative use of AI in the creation of instructional materials.
units.fit_note: P48 also covers instructor review of the materials; this unit requires disclosure only.

units.why: 'Instructors should provide a rationale when disclosing their own genAI use' to 'build trust and model metacognition': an instructor-disclosure practice (P47) that adds reasons-giving.
units.anchor: Instructors should provide a rationale when disclosing their own genAI use in order
units.frag_end: metacognition, intentionality, and transparency for their students
units.policy: Instructors should provide a rationale when disclosing their own genAI use in order to build trust and model metacognition, intentionality, and transparency for their students.
units.fit_note: Adds that the disclosure should carry a rationale to model metacognition and transparency.

units.why: 'Instructors shall disclose their own use, if any, of generative AI in grading' requires telling students about instructor AI use in grading, which is P47 (not P46, since it does not say who assigns grades).
units.anchor: Instructors shall disclose their own use, if any, of generative AI in grading.

units.why: The principles intro says 'Students need to understand the principles guiding GenAI use', framing the guideline's purpose and principles for the institution (P56).
units.anchor: Students need to understand the principles guiding GenAI use in assessments and deliverables.

units.why: Under 'Proficiency', 'students should have a firm grasp of the subject matter' to use GenAI effectively: subject mastery comes before effective AI use, matching P42 in part.
units.anchor: To use GenAI effectively, students should
units.frag_start: To use GenAI effectively, students should
units.frag_end: firm grasp of the subject matter
units.policy: To use GenAI effectively, students should have a firm grasp of the subject matter.
units.fit_note: Framed as a principle for any student, not specifically novices or foundational courses.

units.why: 'Students must take full responsibility for GenAI-generated materials' makes students answerable for AI output they use, matching P29.
units.anchor: Students must take full responsibility for GenAI-generated materials
units.policy: Students must take full responsibility for GenAI-generated materials, ensuring they are accurate and factually sound.
units.fit_note: Responsibility is tied to accuracy of AI-generated content, not only ownership of submitted work.

units.why: 'Generative AI can produce incorrect or misleading information, making verification crucial' states that output is often wrong and must be checked (P31).
units.anchor: accurate and factually sound. Generative AI can produce incorrect or misleading information
units.policy: Generative AI can produce incorrect or misleading information, making verification crucial.

units.why: 'Proper documentation is essential for all non-original ideas and sources' sets a documentation principle for AI use, so P24.
units.anchor: Proper documentation is essential for all non-original ideas and sources, as GenAI
units.policy: Proper documentation is essential for all non-original ideas and sources.

units.why: 'GenAI may create fictional references, also known as hallucinations' warns that AI output can be fabricated, supporting verification (P31).
units.anchor: may create fictional references, also known as
units.policy: GenAI may create fictional references, also known as hallucinations.

units.why: 'When documentation is required, students must follow standard practices for citing sources' fixes how AI use is cited when documentation applies (P24).
units.anchor: students must follow standard practices for citing sources.
units.policy: When documentation is required, students must follow standard practices for citing sources.

units.why: 'Classification Levels of Allowed Use' with four named levels is an explicit tier scheme, P05.
units.anchor: Classification Levels of Allowed Use of GenAI in Assessments and Deliverables
units.policy: The following classification levels determine the permitted use of GenAI in course assessments and deliverables: AI-1 Disallowed, AI-2 Restricted, AI-3 Documented, AI-4 Unrestricted.

units.why: 'The classification of each assessment or deliverable will determine the level of AI use allowed' makes the level per assessment, so the instructor classifies each one (P04), the other type to consider being P05, which is coded on the tier list.
units.anchor: The classification of each assessment or deliverable will determine the level

units.why: 'must adhere to specific transparency, documentation, and accuracy requirements' is a general student duty attached to the levels; closest is P24 (disclosure) though it also names accuracy.
units.anchor: must adhere to specific transparency,
units.policy: Students submitting assessments and deliverables must adhere to specific transparency, documentation, and accuracy requirements.
units.fit_note: Also covers accuracy, not only disclosure.

units.why: AI-1 says GenAI 'tools are strictly prohibited' in the assessment; it is the 'Disallowed' tier of the scheme (P05), not a default ban (P01).
units.anchor: Generative AI tools are strictly prohibited in this assessment or deliverable.

units.why: 'Any use of AI will be considered a violation of academic integrity' sets the consequence for AI-1 work, classifying it as misconduct (P36).
units.anchor: AI will be considered a violation of academic integrity.
units.policy: Under AI-1, any use of AI will be considered a violation of academic integrity.

units.why: AI-2 'students may use AI, but with restrictions and documentation requirements specified by the instructor' is the 'Restricted' tier (P05).
units.anchor: students may use AI, but with restrictions and
units.policy: Under AI-2 Restricted, students may use AI, but with restrictions and documentation requirements specified by the instructor.

units.why: AI-3 'Students can use AI in any manner ... but they must provide appropriate documentation' is the 'Documented' tier (P05).
units.anchor: Students can use AI in any manner for this assessment or deliverable, but they
units.policy: Under AI-3 Documented, students can use AI in any manner for the assessment or deliverable but must provide appropriate documentation for all AI use.

units.why: AI-4 'can be used without restrictions, and documentation is not required' is the 'Unrestricted' tier (P05).
units.anchor: Generative AI tools can be used without restrictions, and documentation is not
units.policy: Under AI-4 Unrestricted, generative AI tools can be used without restrictions and documentation is not required.

units.why: The scope sentence says the guidelines apply to teaching 'not in research with human subjects or otherwise', defining what the policy covers (P61).
units.anchor: educational context, not in research with human subjects or otherwise.
units.frag_end: research with human subjects or otherwise
units.policy: These guidelines apply to assessments and deliverables within the educational context, not in research with human subjects or otherwise.

units.why: 'most commercially available AI systems do not comply with HIPAA or FERPA protections' is a privacy fact that warns about data, P50.
units.anchor: commercially available AI systems do not comply with HIPAA or FERPA protections.

units.why: 'Exercise caution ... to prevent unintended disclosure of confidential or sensitive information' protects personal data when using AI (P50).
units.anchor: Exercise caution when interacting with GenAI platforms to prevent unintended disclosure of
units.policy: Exercise caution when interacting with GenAI platforms to prevent unintended disclosure of confidential or sensitive information.

units.why: 'Always review GenAI-generated content to ensure it does not inadvertently contain sensitive or confidential details' guards against leaked data in output (P50).
units.anchor: Always review GenAI-generated content to ensure it does not inadvertently contain sensitive or
units.policy: Always review GenAI-generated content to ensure it does not inadvertently contain sensitive or confidential details.

units.why: 'GenAI models can inherit biases in the data they were trained on' names bias as a concern (P53).
units.anchor: Understand that GenAI models can inherit biases in the data they were trained on.

units.why: 'Validate the accuracy of information sourced from GenAI by cross-referencing' tells users to verify output (P31).
units.anchor: Validate the accuracy of information sourced from GenAI by cross-referencing it with trusted
units.policy: Validate the accuracy of information sourced from GenAI by cross-referencing it with trusted resources.

units.why: 'Opt for clear and explicit phrasing to improve a GenAI system's understanding of your queries' is prompting advice that no type covers, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Opt for clear and explicit phrasing to improve a GenAI system's understanding of your queries
units.policy: Opt for clear and explicit phrasing to improve a GenAI system's understanding of your queries and reduce potential misunderstandings.
units.uncovered_note: Practical advice on how to phrase prompts so the AI understands the query.

units.why: 'GenAI systems may not fully understand sarcasm, irony, or complex contextual cues' states a limitation of AI; nearest is P31 (output may be wrong) but it concerns understanding, not output accuracy.
units.anchor: GenAI systems may not fully understand sarcasm, irony, or complex contextual cues.
units.fit_note: Describes a comprehension limit of AI rather than wrong or hallucinated output.

units.why: 'Utilize your judgment to critically assess the output from GenAI' asks users to evaluate AI output critically (P31).
units.anchor: Utilize your judgment to critically assess the output from GenAI technologies, particularly for
units.policy: Utilize your judgment to critically assess the output from GenAI technologies, particularly for nuanced or controversial subjects.

units.why: 'GenAI tools are not infallible and should not be the sole basis for significant decisions' keeps human judgment in charge; P32 (AI must not replace thinking) fits better than P73, which is about decisions on individuals.
units.anchor: should not be the sole basis for significant
units.policy: GenAI tools are not infallible and should not be the sole basis for significant decisions.
units.fit_note: Concerns significant decisions generally, not only a student's own problem solving.

units.why: 'Be aware that GenAI technologies can be exploited for sophisticated phishing scams' is security awareness, P75.
units.anchor: Be aware that GenAI technologies can be exploited for sophisticated phishing scams or
units.policy: Be aware that GenAI technologies can be exploited for sophisticated phishing scams or cybersecurity threats.

units.why: 'scrutinize GenAI-generated messages and links ... and report any suspicious activity' to IT Security is a duty to check and report, P75.
units.anchor: Constantly scrutinize GenAI-generated messages and links for authenticity and report any
units.policy: Constantly scrutinize GenAI-generated messages and links for authenticity and report any suspicious activity to the IT Security Office.

units.why: 'Participate in university-offered training sessions' encourages AI-literacy training for the community (P70).
units.anchor: Participate in university-offered training sessions to enhance your understanding of GenAI's
units.policy: Participate in university-offered training sessions to enhance your understanding of GenAI's capabilities, limitations, and associated cybersecurity risks.

units.why: 'Stay updated on institutional guidelines and policies concerning GenAI' asks users to keep up with changing rules, a duty that fits no type exactly, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Stay updated on institutional guidelines and policies concerning GenAI technologies.
units.uncovered_note: Users must keep themselves informed of current institutional AI guidelines.

units.why: 'students must provide documentation regarding their use of generative AI' under AI-2 or AI-3 is a disclosure requirement (P24).
units.anchor: students must provide documentation regarding their use of generative

units.fit_note: Also leaves the choice of format to instructors.

units.why: The appendix says the 'output generated by GenAI is not subject to expert review' and references 'may not always be accurate', warning students to verify sources (P31).

units.frag_start: It's important to note that while GenAI content may contain references to primary

units.policy: The output generated by GenAI is not subject to expert review, and the source references may not always be accurate.

units.why: 'all factual statements in the work must be attributed to the original sources' when primary citations are mandated sets a citation duty (P24).
units.anchor: all factual statements in the work must

units.policy: Where primary source citations are mandated, all factual statements in the work must be attributed to the original sources following standard prescribed citation styles.

units.why: Summary statements 'should include details such as the name and URL of the AI system ... the prompts' lists what an AI citation contains, matching P25.
units.anchor: include details such as the name and URL of the AI system,
units.policy: Summary statements should include details such as the name and URL of the AI system, the specific purpose for which generative AI was employed, the prompts that were used, and how the AI-generated output was utilized or modified.

units.why: The sample 'I hereby acknowledge the use of [insert AI system(s) and link]' gives students acknowledgement template wording (P25).
units.anchor: I hereby acknowledge the use of [insert AI system(s) and link] for
units.policy: Students may acknowledge AI use with the template: I hereby acknowledge the use of [AI system(s) and link] for [particular use]; the prompts employed encompass [list of prompts]; the outcomes were utilized to [clarify the use].

notes: Coded only the AI sections of a 465k-character Curriculum Guide (syllabus requirement near line 2429, checklist line 1767, GenAI guidelines at line 5497, change log at lines 8221-8308). Repeated change-log mentions of the syllabus-statement and plagiarism changes were skipped as repeats.
